parole.testo: From New Latin, feminine of babuinus, from French babouin.

parole.significato: Any of several compounds of barium, especially barium sulphate and barium hydroxide.
parole.testo: From New Latin baryta, from 18c. Latinization of French barote, 1782 coinage from Ancient Greek βαρύτης (barútēs, “heaviness”), from βαρύς (barús) + -της (-tēs).

parole.significato: A chemical element (symbol Cr) with an atomic number of 24: a steely-grey, lustrous, hard and brittle transition metal.
parole.testo: From New Latin, from French chrome (from Ancient Greek χρῶμα (khrôma, “color”)) + -ium. So called because of the striking colors of its compounds.

parole.significato: Any arboreal marsupial of most genera of the family Phalangeridae, native to northern Australia, New Guinea, and Indone…
parole.testo: From New Latin Cuscus, former genus name, ultimately (probably via French and Dutch koeskoes) from a local word for the marsupials in a language of the Moluccas.

parole.significato: A complication of pregnancy characterized by seizures and coma due to hypertension.
parole.testo: Borrowed from New Latin eclampsia, from French éclampsie, from Ancient Greek ἔκλᾰμψῐς (éklămpsĭs, “sudden development, violent onset”, literally “brightness”), from ἐκλᾰ́μπω (eklắmpō, “to shine or beam forth; to burst forth violently”) + -σῐς (-sĭs, nominal suffix).

parole.significato: Synonym of foraminifer (“any of a large group of aquatic amoeboid protists of the subphylum Foraminifera, characterized…
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from New Latin Foraminifera (subphylum name), from French foraminifère (“foraminifer, foraminifera”), from French Foraminifères, coined by the French naturalist Alcide d’Orbigny (1802–1857) in an 1826 article. Foraminifère is derived from Latin forāmina (“apertures, holes”) + -fer
From New Latin glucina, from French glucine, from Ancient Greek γλυκύς (glukús, “sweet”) + -um, in reference to the sweet taste of some of its salts.

parole.significato: In preparation for the main matter; initial, introductory, preparatory.
parole.testo: Borrowed from New Latin praelīmināris, formed from prae- (“before”) + līmen (“threshold”) + -āris (adjectival suffix); compare Latin līmināris (“of or belonging to a threshold”). Compare French préliminaire.

parole.significato: A bladder-like pouch on the head of schizophoran flies that by expanding enables the fly to emerge from its puparium.
parole.testo: Borrowed from New Latin ptilīnum, itself an adaptation of the French ptiline.

parole.significato: Of, pertaining to, or suffering from scurvy.
parole.testo: From early New Latin scorbūticus (“pertaining to scurvy”), from scorbūtus (“scurvy”), from French scorbut, of Germanic origin.
From New Latin scorbūtus, from French scorbut. Doublet of scorbut and scurvy.

parole.significato: A water-soluble organic compound, CO(NH₂)₂, formed by the metabolism of proteins and excreted in the urine.
parole.testo: From New Latin, from French urée, from Ancient Greek οὖρον (oûron, “urine”).
